texts: Long-term survival after repair of truncus arteriosus is about 60 percent at 20 years: C.
Early mortality has fallen to around 5 to 10 percent, but late deaths continue, often linked to reoperations for conduit replacement and to truncal valve disease.
Truncal valve insufficiency at repair, an interrupted arch and coronary anomalies are the main risk factors; replacement of a truncal valve that was competent at repair is uncommon.
In the picture, six of the ten hotels still stand after twenty years.
